purpose: The Engineering Assurance release this repository adopts, and the digests of the artifacts it actually reads from that release. Component version pins are NOT restated here: the packaged compatibility matrix is their authority and a second copy would drift from it.
matrix_authority: engineering_assurance/compatibility-matrix.json in the installed distribution. scripts/check_shared_pins.py observes the local toolchain and delegates every verdict to engineering_assurance.compatibility.
registry: Every npm component resolves from the public npm registry (registry.npmjs.org). The internal npm.ix mirror must not appear in any requirement, pin, lockfile, or .npmrc, and is not an oracle for whether a release landed. Querying an @agent-ix package needs --@agent-ix:registry=https://registry.npmjs.org; a bare --registry does not override the scoped .npmrc entry.

engineering_assurance.release_form: git tag v0.2.0, a source distribution; the tag is the released artifact

consumed_artifacts.why: scripts/check_shared_pins.py imports load_matrix, classify_all and accepted from this module and delegates every component verdict to it. It is the one artifact this repository still reads out of the release on every `make pins`, so it is the one that carries a digest.

The authority on which component versions are pinned, and on which versions are named incompatible. Deliberately carries no digest here: it is expected to advance as the matrix is re-accepted, and pinning its bytes locally would make this repository a second acceptance authority.

known_drift: engineering-assurance v0.2.0 packages compatibility-matrix.json with accepted.state = pending_human_acceptance and ships no human_acceptance_recorded predicate. Both landed on main after the tag and no v0.2.1 was cut. Filed as agent-ix/engineering-assurance#20. scripts/check_shared_pins.py reports the acceptance state the installed package records and gates only on the local toolchain, so an absent field is never read as an approval in either direction.
Pinning a branch head to obtain the acceptance record is exactly what the release discipline forbids, so this repository does not.

FR-003 (Kani obligation lowering) and FR-004 (vacuity and rejection evidence) are specified and not implemented at this candidate revision: there is no Kani or vacuity code under src/, and every TM-001 row is 🚧 Planned. This migration preserves the specification and the planned status and does not manufacture a producer for behaviour that does not exist. The generation producer reports on the oracle, harness and strategy slices that do.
consumed_artifacts_note: Four artifacts were pinned here by digest until the pre-stable preservation release (engineering-assurance#7): the verification-semantics module, the PGM-01 compatibility-view schema, and the two packaged PGM-01 positive-control fixtures. Every one of them was consumed only by the retained-evidence reader under scripts/, which is deleted along with the records it read. Leaving them would have made this file's own purpose statement — the digests of the artifacts it actually reads — false, and would have left artifact_digest_mismatches re-hashing files nothing in this repository opens. They are replaced by a live pin on compatibility.py rather than removed outright, so the digest check keeps a subject and does not become vacuous.

schemas.why: Three schemas remain under schemas/ and all three are live domain contracts, not evidence machinery. src/oracle.rs includes each at compile time and the crate validates what it generates against them.

live.why: src/oracle.rs includes it as PGM_SCHEMA and the generator validates every derivation manifest it emits against it. It is also part of the generator's own executable_digest. The `pgm01` in its filename names the programme that governed the shape, not the retained records that were deleted: a filename is not a dependency, and this file was measured live rather than inherited from a sibling's freeze list.
the shape of generated Rust, included by src/oracle.rs and validated against in tests/oracle_generation.rs
the shape of the generated source-region map, for the same reason

schemas.deleted: The foundation evidence input and manifest schemas were frozen, not live: they were kept only because retained collection inputs and evidence manifests named them by SHA-256. The records that named them are deleted, so there is no longer a reference for the freeze to protect and the two schemas went with them. Nothing executable referenced either at any point. Their names are not repeated here: tests/shared_assurance.rs runs a census asserting that no code or configuration file in this repository mentions them, and this register is configuration.
